key_insight: ConQUESTA prunes quantum neural networks by jointly considering task accuracy and hardware-aware compiler cost, so it removes entanglers without exploding SWAPs, depth, or two-qubit gates.
engineering_relevance: This makes QNN deployment more practical on sparse quantum hardware by turning pruning into a topology-aware post-training optimization problem with explicit accuracy constraints.
method: Screens candidate entanglers using both saliency and estimated compiler cost.
Searches complete pruning masks under a user-defined accuracy constraint rather than ranking gates one-by-one.
Transpiles each mask as a whole across multiple coupling topologies to account for routing effects.
evidence_signal: Across 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit QNNs at 55% pruning, ConQUESTA achieved mean resource reductions of 61.6% on Breast Cancer, 72.0% on Digits01, and 82.2% on Iris, and improved fixed-mask feasibility from 16/24 to 22/24 runs.
watch_item: The approach may be computationally heavier than simple ranking methods because it evaluates many whole-mask candidates under multiple hardware topologies.
paper_title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
